QT about 357 ms, Bazett QTc about 384 ms (normal, reassuring on escitalopram). This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, regular (RR 800-890 ms), with upright P waves and PR about 162 ms. Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular (RR 858-904 ms), with upright P waves in II/aVF and PR about 160 ms. QRS narrow at 80 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +57 degrees (normal). Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm, regular (RR 1112-1168 ms), with upright P waves and a PR interval of about 178 ms (normal). QRS 88 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -6 degrees (normal). Sinus tachycardia at 141 bpm. Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, regular (RR 944-982 ms), with upright P waves and PR about 184 ms (within normal limits). QRS 96 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +68 degrees (normal). Atrial fibrillation with a moderately rapid, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean rate about 99 bpm (RR 386-1092 ms, RMSSD 264 ms). items.explanation: 80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (9/12/2025 through 5/28/2026). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation (Class 1 for CHA2DS2-VASc >=2) is absent; antiplatelet therapy is not a substitute. Needs review for initiation of a DOAC or warfarin.

Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (4/8/2026) are normal. Prescriber review of escitalopram and a repeat ECG are required.

95-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation/flutter on long-term amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug; the current order runs 8/22/2026 to 1/5/2027. Prescriber review of amiodarone and an up-to-date ECG are required.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 4/10/2026. Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/1/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/15/2026. Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/10/2026, so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/24/2026. Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG is due within 14 days of the start, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since the start (the most recent tracing is 104253928 from 3/9/2025), but the due date is after the 9/24/2026 evaluation time, so the requirement is not yet due.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in all cardiology clinic notes (7/19/2025 through 6/12/2026). Chart problem list includes congestive heart failure / acute systolic heart failure with other primary cardiomyopathy and essential hypertension, giving CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (CHF 1, hypertension 1; age 48, male, no diabetes, no prior stroke, no vascular disease). CHA2DS2-VASc >=2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, but current medications are only famotidine and pantoprazole and no anticoagulant order is active at the evaluation time. Needs review for anticoagulation.

At the 9/1/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit Dr. Kessler documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. An INR of 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026 (Observation d6b3bad5), 4 days after the dose change, so the monitoring requirement was completed within the required time.

In the anticoagulation clinic telephone note of 9/10/2026 the clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol after a home INR of 3.4. Clinic pharmacists may adjust warfarin under the standing order, so this is a qualifying dose change and the 3/1/2026 memo required an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. No INR has been resulted since 8/22/2026 (INR 2.6); the home INR of 3.4 preceded and prompted the change and cannot satisfy it. The follow-up INR is overdue as of the 9/24/2026 evaluation.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on the problem list and in every cardiology clinic note (10/10/2025 through 7/28/2026). Risk factors: essential hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, coronary atherosclerosis of a native coronary artery (vascular disease) 1 = CHA2DS2-VASc 3, a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation. His only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; no anticoagulant order is active at the evaluation time. The chart carries a remote coded diagnosis of hemorrhage complicating a procedure, but no active bleeding or documented decision to withhold anticoagulation, so this needs prescriber review.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on the problem list. She also carries cerebral infarction due to embolism with residual hemiplegia/hemiparesis and facial weakness, and essential hypertension, giving CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (prior stroke 2, hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female 1). Anticoagulation is strongly recommended (Class 1, secondary stroke prevention), but current medications are famotidine, metoprolol tartrate and carvedilol only, with no anticoagulant order active at the evaluation time. Her 3/14/2025 ECG showed sinus rhythm, which does not change the indication in paroxysmal AF. Needs review for anticoagulation.

74-year-old man with atrial flutter on apixaban 5 mg twice daily; the current order was written 8/20/2026 and runs to 12/28/2026. Outside records reviewed on 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, and state that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite that, apixaban was re-ordered at the 8/20/2026 clinic visit (and he also remains on aspirin 81 mg plus clopidogrel 75 mg, i.e. triple therapy) with no documented decision that the bleeding source was treated or that anticoagulation could safely resume. Prescriber review of whether to continue apixaban, and of concomitant antiplatelet therapy, is required.

Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously active for this 65-year-old man with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation and flutter. At the 7/15/2026 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban 20 mg daily order (7/15/2026 to 12/25/2026) was left active alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily order (7/15/2026 to 12/26/2026), and the visit note lists both drugs as current medications. Both orders still cover the evaluation date, so the patient is prescribed duplicate full-dose anticoagulation with a high bleeding risk (he also has CLL). The rivaroxaban order must be discontinued.

The 6/10/2026 cardiology clinic note states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular rhythm with no discernible P waves and ventricular rates of about 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; the chart rhythm documentation needs correction and the rapid AF needs clinical review.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily is a QT watch-list medication and the current order (4/23/2026 to 1/2/2027) is active at the evaluation time. His most recent ECG (108018814, 10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT about 487 ms and Bazett-corrected QTc about 519 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo. 79-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug; the current order runs 7/29/2026 to 1/5/2027. Most recent potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (4/20/2026) are normal. He is also on warfarin (amiodarone interaction). Prescriber review of amiodarone dosing and repeat ECG required.

Sinus rhythm at 104 bpm, regular (RR 568-586 ms), with well-formed upright P waves in II and aVF and PR about 148 ms - no atrial fibrillation on this tracing despite the documented paroxysmal AF. Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm with a regular RR interval and an upright P wave before each QRS, PR about 128 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +36 degrees (normal). QT about 338 ms giving a Bazett QTc of about 456 ms, at the upper limit of normal and partly rate-related. Only one ECG exists for this patient, so no prior comparison is possible.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 144 bpm and an irregularly irregular RR interval (348-650 ms). Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 864-884 ms) with a low-amplitude atrial deflection before every QRS at a constant PR interval of about 148 ms - sinus rhythm; the P wave is upright in lead I but flat to slightly negative in II/aVF, suggesting a low atrial/leftward P axis or limb-lead placement variation rather than a change of mechanism. Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, regular (RR 596-630 ms), with upright P waves and a PR interval of about 120 ms. QRS is narrow at 72 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +4 degrees (normal). Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular (RR 820-840 ms), with upright P waves in II and aVF and PR about 152 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +22 degrees (normal). Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, regular (RR 774-804 ms), with prominent upright P waves in II/aVF and PR about 174 ms. QRS is narrow at 68 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +64 degrees (normal). QT about 399 ms with Bazett QTc about 451 ms. Rhythm is unchanged and no bundle branch block is present on either tracing.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, RR almost perfectly regular (494-504 ms) with a consistent upright P wave before each QRS, PR about 170 ms. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +51 degrees (normal). QT about 275 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 389 ms. Compared with the prior tracing of 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, PR 182 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc about 396 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm, regular (RR 1074-1116 ms), with upright P waves in II and aVF. The PR interval is prolonged at about 220 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +7 degrees (normal). QT about 401 ms, Bazett QTc about 382 ms (normal). The prior ECG of 11/30/2024 was also sinus bradycardia at 51 bpm with a borderline PR of about 200 ms, QRS 82 ms and QTc about 363 ms; rhythm, bundle branch conduction and QTc are unchanged (first-degree AV block is not one of the reportable change categories).

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 153 bpm and a chaotically irregular RR interval (288-580 ms). No P waves or organised atrial activity are present, so the PR interval is not measurable. QRS 98 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -20 degrees (normal). QT about 271 ms with Bazett QTc about 432 ms. The prior ECG from the previous evening (107374881, 9/12/2025) showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with clear P waves, PR about 158 ms and one premature beat, so atrial fibrillation is new (NEW_AF). QTc is essentially unchanged (about 414 to 432 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm with mild sinus arrhythmia (RR 788-922 ms), upright P waves in II/aVF and PR about 178 ms. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +11 degrees (normal). QT about 359 ms, Bazett QTc about 397 ms (normal). The prior ECG of 11/21/2025 was also sinus (67 bpm, PR about 158 ms, QRS 90 ms) but with a much longer QT (about 505 ms) and QTc of about 535 ms, so the corrected QT has shortened by roughly 140 ms (QTC_DECREASE_60). Rhythm and conduction are unchanged; this tracing agrees with the 11/23/2025 note documenting sinus rhythm.

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, regular (RR 780-840 ms), with upright P waves and a PR interval of about 190 ms (upper normal, not first-degree AV block). QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +54 degrees (normal). QT about 372 ms with Bazett QTc about 413 ms (normal). This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm with an almost fixed RR interval (536-542 ms) and a clear upright P wave before every QRS, PR about 176 ms; there is no atrial flutter on this tracing despite the coded history of atrial flutter (no sawtooth waves, and the atrial and ventricular rates are 1:1). QRS 92 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +35 degrees (normal). QT about 279 ms, Bazett QTc about 381 ms. The prior ECG of 7/4/2022 was essentially identical (sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, PR about 182 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc about 375 ms); no changes.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with an underlying regular cycle of about 980 ms interrupted by one premature beat and a compensatory pause (RR 540 then 1370 ms); P waves precede the sinus beats with a PR interval of about 194 ms. QRS 98 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -31 degrees, i.e. borderline left axis deviation. QT about 354 ms with Bazett QTc about 358 ms (normal). There is no atrial fibrillation on this tracing, although paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is on the problem list. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

Regular sinus rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 838-884 ms) with an atrial deflection before every QRS at a constant PR interval of about 144 ms. QRS 88 ms with no bundle branch block. The frontal plane shows a globally negative lead I and aVL with a strongly positive aVR and negative aVF, giving a computed axis of about -173 degrees (extreme axis deviation); together with the inverted P wave in lead I and normal precordial R-wave progression this pattern is typical of right/left arm lead reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation, and repeat recording with correct electrode placement is advised. QT about 357 ms, Bazett QTc about 384 ms (normal, reassuring on escitalopram). This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, regular (RR 800-890 ms), with upright P waves and PR about 162 ms. QRS 100 ms - slightly wide but not meeting bundle branch block criteria; frontal axis about +37 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with broad T waves: QT about 509 ms and Bazett QTc about 550 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in a patient on citalopram 40 mg daily. The prior ECG of 6/17/2020 showed sinus tachycardia at 132 bpm with QTc about 435 ms, so the corrected QT has increased by about 115 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60). Rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular (RR 858-904 ms), with upright P waves in II/aVF and PR about 160 ms. QRS narrow at 80 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +57 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is abnormal and prolonged, with biphasic/low-amplitude T waves in the lateral and inferior leads and deep T inversion in V2-V3; tangent-method measurement across leads gives QT about 503 ms and a Bazett QTc of about 536 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in a patient taking escitalopram. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm, regular (RR 1112-1168 ms), with upright P waves and a PR interval of about 178 ms (normal). QRS 88 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -6 degrees (normal). QT about 381 ms with Bazett QTc about 358 ms (normal). The prior ECG of 12/13/2018 showed sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with a longer PR of about 216 ms (first-degree AV block) and QTc about 389 ms; rhythm, bundle branch conduction and QTc show no reportable change.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm (RR 862-902 ms) with normal upright P waves, PR about 132 ms. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +46 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is markedly prolonged: QT about 487 ms giving a Bazett QTc of about 519 ms, above the 500 ms threshold while the patient takes escitalopram. The prior ECG of 11/23/2022 showed sinus rhythm at 75 bpm with QTc about 354 ms, so the QTc has increased by about 165 ms - a QTC_INCREASE_60 change. Rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 141 bpm. The RR interval is now regular (402-454 ms) and a discrete low-amplitude upright P wave is identifiable in II/aVF before every QRS, well after the end of the T wave, with a PR interval of about 110 ms; atrial and ventricular rates are 1:1, so this is not atrial flutter. QRS 80 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -2 degrees (normal). QT about 271 ms, Bazett QTc about 415 ms. The prior ECG of 7/11/2022 showed atrial fibrillation at about 110 bpm with a chaotically irregular RR interval (380-824 ms) and no P waves, so the atrial fibrillation has resolved (RESOLVED_AF). QTc is unchanged (about 418 to 415 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, regular (RR 710-744 ms), with upright P waves and PR about 184 ms (normal). QRS 100 ms - mildly widened but not meeting criteria for right or left bundle branch block; frontal axis about +34 degrees (normal). QT about 372 ms with Bazett QTc about 437 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, regular (RR 650-668 ms), with upright P waves in II and aVF. The PR interval is prolonged at about 210-225 ms, consistent with first-degree AV block. QRS is narrow at 78 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -18 degrees (normal). QT about 338 ms, Bazett QTc about 417 ms. The prior ECG of 5/16/2021 showed sinus rhythm at 87 bpm with a normal PR of about 152 ms, QRS 80 ms and QTc about 393 ms; the PR has lengthened but rhythm, bundle branch conduction and QTc show no reportable change category.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm (RR 954-1196 ms) with upright P waves and a prolonged PR interval of about 222 ms - first-degree AV block. Frontal axis about -21 degrees (normal). QT about 431 ms, Bazett QTc about 435 ms. The prior ECG of 6/3/2024 showed the identical pattern (sinus 68 bpm, PR about 220 ms, QRS 128 ms with left bundle branch block, QTc about 441 ms), so there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm with a regular RR interval (492-500 ms) and a discrete upright P wave before each QRS, PR about 150 ms. QRS duration 86 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +68 degrees (normal). QT about 285 ms, Bazett QTc about 405 ms (normal). This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, regular, with upright P waves in II and aVF and PR about 158 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +58 degrees (normal). QT about 319 ms with Bazett QTc about 415 ms. The prior tracing taken 34 seconds earlier the same morning (102910502, 8/23/2021) was essentially identical (sinus 100 bpm, PR 152 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc about 408 ms), so there are no interval changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with a very regular RR interval (1144-1178 ms). QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block, tall R waves in V6; frontal axis about +36 degrees (normal). QT about 435 ms, Bazett QTc about 404 ms. The prior ECG of 5/22/2023 also showed sinus rhythm (57 bpm with one premature beat, PR about 150 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc about 369 ms); no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, RR very regular (492-496 ms), upright P waves with PR about 136 ms. The QRS is now narrow at 92 ms with only a small terminal r in V1 (incomplete right bundle branch block pattern at most) and no complete bundle branch block. Prominent S waves in I and aVL with a net negative lead I give a rightward frontal axis of about +143 degrees. QT about 297 ms, Bazett QTc about 422 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (106516875, 01:33) showed a QRS of about 152 ms with a broad terminal R in V1 and wide S waves in I and V6 - complete right bundle branch block - which has resolved on this 14:38 tracing, hence RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK. QTc fell from about 476 to 422 ms (less than 60 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, regular (RR 944-982 ms), with upright P waves and PR about 184 ms (within normal limits). QRS 96 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +68 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is prolonged: QT about 528 ms with a Bazett QTc of about 537 ms, exceeding the 500 ms review threshold in a patient on amiodarone. The prior ECG of 6/7/2025 (sinus bradycardia 47 bpm, PR about 182 ms, QRS 96 ms, QTc about 407 ms) was taken before amiodarone was started, so the QTc has risen by about 130 ms - QTC_INCREASE_60. Rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

Atrial fibrillation with a moderately rapid, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean rate about 99 bpm (RR 386-1092 ms, RMSSD 264 ms). No organised P waves are seen in any lead and there is no consistent atrial deflection in the TP segments, so no measurable PR interval. QRS is narrow at 78 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -54 degrees (left axis deviation). QT about 328 ms, Bazett QTc about 421 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible. It corroborates the coded diagnosis of atrial fibrillation for which he is anticoagulated with warfarin.

items.explanation: 80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (9/12/2025 through 5/28/2026). Chart also documents hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, type 2 diabetes, prior cerebral infarction/TIA and atherosclerotic coronary disease, giving CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (CHF 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, diabetes 1, prior stroke/TIA 2, vascular disease 1, female 1). Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin only, with no anticoagulant order active at the evaluation time. Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation (Class 1 for CHA2DS2-VASc >=2) is absent; antiplatelet therapy is not a substitute. Needs review for initiation of a DOAC or warfarin.

35-year-old woman on citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication; the current order runs 5/29/2026 to 12/25/2026 and the dose is above the 20 mg maximum usually advised when QT prolongation is present. Her most recent ECG (104821039, 11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT about 509 ms and Bazett QTc about 550 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold; the previous ECG (6/17/2020) had a QTc of about 435 ms. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (1/21/2026) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (12/1/2023) are normal, and she also has hypothyroidism and type 1 diabetes. Prescriber review of citalopram dose and a current ECG are required.

44-year-old man with coronary disease and a coronary stent on escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication; the current order runs 7/8/2026 to 12/29/2026. His most recent (and only) ECG (101538691, 3/8/2026, obtained as the post-start monitoring ECG) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with markedly abnormal repolarisation, QT about 503 ms and Bazett QTc about 536 ms, above the 500 ms review threshold. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (4/8/2026) are normal. Prescriber review of escitalopram and a repeat ECG are required.

95-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation/flutter on long-term amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug; the current order runs 8/22/2026 to 1/5/2027. Her most recent ECG (101515306, 4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with first-degree AV block (PR about 210 ms), QT about 537 ms and Bazett QTc about 526 ms, above the 500 ms review threshold (the 4/6/2022 tracing in AF had a QTc of about 421 ms). Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (2/14/2026) are at the low-normal end. She also takes metoprolol and warfarin. Prescriber review of amiodarone and an up-to-date ECG are required.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was newly started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 3/2/2026. Because the start was on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 3/7/2026 (sinus rhythm 81 bpm, QTc about 381 ms), 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met within the required time.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 11/10/2025. The start date falls between 9/1/2025 and 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies and an ECG was due by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was completed in time. (That ECG showed QTc about 537 ms and is the basis of a separate QT safety item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2/12/2026. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was recorded on 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start, meeting the requirement in time. (Its QTc of about 536 ms is the basis of a separate QT safety item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 4/10/2026. Because the start was after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, by 4/24/2026. No ECG exists in that window: the only tracing (107859369) was not recorded until 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start and outside the required window, so the requirement was not satisfied on time and remains past due for documentation/review. The 4/29/2026 ECG itself showed sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with QTc about 384 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/1/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/15/2026. No ECG has been obtained since the start; the only tracing in the chart is 106035722 from 12/25/2025, which predates the start. The required post-start ECG is overdue as of the 9/24/2026 evaluation.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/10/2026, so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/24/2026. No ECG for this patient exists in the chart, but the nurse telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing falls inside the required window and could have satisfied the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG is due within 14 days of the start, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since the start (the most recent tracing is 104253928 from 3/9/2025), but the due date is after the 9/24/2026 evaluation time, so the requirement is not yet due.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in all cardiology clinic notes (7/19/2025 through 6/12/2026). Chart problem list includes congestive heart failure / acute systolic heart failure with other primary cardiomyopathy and essential hypertension, giving CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (CHF 1, hypertension 1; age 48, male, no diabetes, no prior stroke, no vascular disease). CHA2DS2-VASc >=2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, but current medications are only famotidine and pantoprazole and no anticoagulant order is active at the evaluation time. Needs review for anticoagulation.

At the 9/1/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit Dr. Kessler documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. An INR of 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026 (Observation d6b3bad5), 4 days after the dose change, so the monitoring requirement was completed within the required time.

In the anticoagulation clinic telephone note of 9/10/2026 the clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol after a home INR of 3.4. Clinic pharmacists may adjust warfarin under the standing order, so this is a qualifying dose change and the 3/1/2026 memo required an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. No INR has been resulted since 8/22/2026 (INR 2.6); the home INR of 3.4 preceded and prompted the change and cannot satisfy it. The follow-up INR is overdue as of the 9/24/2026 evaluation.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on the problem list and in every cardiology clinic note (10/10/2025 through 7/28/2026). Risk factors: essential hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, coronary atherosclerosis of a native coronary artery (vascular disease) 1 = CHA2DS2-VASc 3, a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation. His only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; no anticoagulant order is active at the evaluation time. The chart carries a remote coded diagnosis of hemorrhage complicating a procedure, but no active bleeding or documented decision to withhold anticoagulation, so this needs prescriber review.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on the problem list. She also carries cerebral infarction due to embolism with residual hemiplegia/hemiparesis and facial weakness, and essential hypertension, giving CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (prior stroke 2, hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female 1). Anticoagulation is strongly recommended (Class 1, secondary stroke prevention), but current medications are famotidine, metoprolol tartrate and carvedilol only, with no anticoagulant order active at the evaluation time. Her 3/14/2025 ECG showed sinus rhythm, which does not change the indication in paroxysmal AF. Needs review for anticoagulation.

74-year-old man with atrial flutter on apixaban 5 mg twice daily; the current order was written 8/20/2026 and runs to 12/28/2026. Outside records reviewed on 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, and state that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite that, apixaban was re-ordered at the 8/20/2026 clinic visit (and he also remains on aspirin 81 mg plus clopidogrel 75 mg, i.e. triple therapy) with no documented decision that the bleeding source was treated or that anticoagulation could safely resume. Prescriber review of whether to continue apixaban, and of concomitant antiplatelet therapy, is required.

Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously active for this 65-year-old man with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation and flutter. At the 7/15/2026 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban 20 mg daily order (7/15/2026 to 12/25/2026) was left active alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily order (7/15/2026 to 12/26/2026), and the visit note lists both drugs as current medications. Both orders still cover the evaluation date, so the patient is prescribed duplicate full-dose anticoagulation with a high bleeding risk (he also has CLL). The rivaroxaban order must be discontinued.

The 6/10/2026 cardiology clinic note states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular rhythm with no discernible P waves and ventricular rates of about 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; the chart rhythm documentation needs correction and the rapid AF needs clinical review.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily is a QT watch-list medication and the current order (4/23/2026 to 1/2/2027) is active at the evaluation time. His most recent ECG (108018814, 10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT about 487 ms and Bazett-corrected QTc about 519 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo. Most recent electrolytes are normal (potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL, both 8/23/2025). The 5/14/2024 note describing the 10/8/2023 ECG as having an acceptable QT is not consistent with this measurement. Prescriber review of escitalopram and a repeat ECG are required.

79-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug; the current order runs 7/29/2026 to 1/5/2027. His most recent ECG (106885519, 11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT about 528 ms and Bazett QTc about 537 ms, above the 500 ms review threshold; the preceding ECG (6/7/2025, before amiodarone was started) had a QTc of about 407 ms, so this is a marked drug-associated increase. Most recent potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (4/20/2026) are normal. He is also on warfarin (amiodarone interaction). Prescriber review of amiodarone dosing and repeat ECG required.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with mild sinus arrhythmia (RR 656-856 ms). Upright P waves in II/aVF preceding every QRS, PR about 198 ms (upper normal, no AV block). Narrow QRS 78 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +47 degrees (normal). QT about 329 ms, Bazett QTc about 381 ms - normal despite concurrent citalopram. No prior ECG in the chart for comparison. Matches the 3/7/2026 clinic note documenting sinus rhythm.

Sinus rhythm at 104 bpm, regular (RR 568-586 ms), with well-formed upright P waves in II and aVF and PR about 148 ms - no atrial fibrillation on this tracing despite the documented paroxysmal AF. QRS 94 ms without bundle branch block; frontal axis about +38 degrees (normal). QT about 356 ms with Bazett QTc about 467 ms, borderline prolonged. On the prior ECG of 6/20/2025 (sinus tachycardia 147 bpm, PR about 124 ms, QRS 94 ms) the QTc was about 385 ms, so the corrected QT has increased by about 80 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60); rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm with a regular RR interval and an upright P wave before each QRS, PR about 128 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +36 degrees (normal). QT about 338 ms giving a Bazett QTc of about 456 ms, at the upper limit of normal and partly rate-related. Only one ECG exists for this patient, so no prior comparison is possible.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 144 bpm and an irregularly irregular RR interval (348-650 ms). There are no P waves and no organised atrial activity, so the PR interval is not measurable. QRS 96 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -1 degree (normal). QT about 282 ms, Bazett QTc about 437 ms. The prior tracing from earlier the same evening (107914094, 6/10/2026 17:13) already showed atrial fibrillation at about 139 bpm with QTc about 437 ms, so there is no interval or rhythm change between them. Note that the 6/10/2026 clinic note recorded 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which both same-day tracings contradict.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 864-884 ms) with a low-amplitude atrial deflection before every QRS at a constant PR interval of about 148 ms - sinus rhythm; the P wave is upright in lead I but flat to slightly negative in II/aVF, suggesting a low atrial/leftward P axis or limb-lead placement variation rather than a change of mechanism. QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -25 degrees (normal). QT about 408 ms, Bazett QTc about 437 ms. The prior ECG of 4/27/2025 showed the same sinus mechanism at 60 bpm (QRS 80 ms, QTc about 405 ms) but with a markedly different, extreme frontal axis consistent with limb-lead reversal on that tracing; rhythm, conduction and QTc are otherwise unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, regular (RR 596-630 ms), with upright P waves and a PR interval of about 120 ms. QRS is narrow at 72 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +4 degrees (normal). QT about 299 ms with Bazett QTc about 381 ms (normal). This is the only ECG in the chart for this patient, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular (RR 820-840 ms), with upright P waves in II and aVF and PR about 152 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +22 degrees (normal). The T wave is followed by a low-amplitude U wave, but tangent-method measurement in multiple leads gives QT about 375 ms and a Bazett QTc of about 411 ms, i.e. normal and below the 500 ms watch-list threshold. Only one ECG exists for this patient, so no prior comparison is possible; it predates the 8/1/2026 escitalopram start.

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with mild sinus arrhythmia (RR 976-1082 ms) and upright P waves before each QRS, PR about 116 ms. The prior ECG of 3/8/2025 was also sinus (62 bpm, PR about 120 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc about 425 ms); no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, extremely regular (RR 716-726 ms), with upright P waves and PR about 160 ms. QRS narrow at 70 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +53 degrees (normal). QT about 341 ms with Bazett QTc about 402 ms (normal). This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, regular (RR 774-804 ms), with prominent upright P waves in II/aVF and PR about 174 ms. QRS is narrow at 68 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +64 degrees (normal). QT about 399 ms with Bazett QTc about 451 ms. The prior ECG of 2/2/2020 showed sinus rhythm at 75 bpm with a wider QRS of about 110 ms (not meeting bundle branch block criteria), diffusely inverted low-amplitude T waves and a much longer QTc of about 530-550 ms; the corrected QT has therefore shortened by roughly 80-100 ms (QTC_DECREASE_60). Rhythm is unchanged and no bundle branch block is present on either tracing.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, RR almost perfectly regular (494-504 ms) with a consistent upright P wave before each QRS, PR about 170 ms. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +51 degrees (normal). QT about 275 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 389 ms. Compared with the prior tracing of 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, PR 182 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc about 396 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm, regular (RR 1074-1116 ms), with upright P waves in II and aVF. The PR interval is prolonged at about 220 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +7 degrees (normal). QT about 401 ms, Bazett QTc about 382 ms (normal). The prior ECG of 11/30/2024 was also sinus bradycardia at 51 bpm with a borderline PR of about 200 ms, QRS 82 ms and QTc about 363 ms; rhythm, bundle branch conduction and QTc are unchanged (first-degree AV block is not one of the reportable change categories).

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 153 bpm and a chaotically irregular RR interval (288-580 ms). No P waves or organised atrial activity are present, so the PR interval is not measurable. QRS 98 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -20 degrees (normal). QT about 271 ms with Bazett QTc about 432 ms. The prior ECG from the previous evening (107374881, 9/12/2025) showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with clear P waves, PR about 158 ms and one premature beat, so atrial fibrillation is new (NEW_AF). QTc is essentially unchanged (about 414 to 432 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm with mild sinus arrhythmia (RR 788-922 ms), upright P waves in II/aVF and PR about 178 ms. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +11 degrees (normal). QT about 359 ms, Bazett QTc about 397 ms (normal). The prior ECG of 11/21/2025 was also sinus (67 bpm, PR about 158 ms, QRS 90 ms) but with a much longer QT (about 505 ms) and QTc of about 535 ms, so the corrected QT has shortened by roughly 140 ms (QTC_DECREASE_60). Rhythm and conduction are unchanged; this tracing agrees with the 11/23/2025 note documenting sinus rhythm.

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, regular (RR 780-840 ms), with upright P waves and a PR interval of about 190 ms (upper normal, not first-degree AV block). QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +54 degrees (normal). QT about 372 ms with Bazett QTc about 413 ms (normal). This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm with an almost fixed RR interval (536-542 ms) and a clear upright P wave before every QRS, PR about 176 ms; there is no atrial flutter on this tracing despite the coded history of atrial flutter (no sawtooth waves, and the atrial and ventricular rates are 1:1). QRS 92 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +35 degrees (normal). QT about 279 ms, Bazett QTc about 381 ms. The prior ECG of 7/4/2022 was essentially identical (sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, PR about 182 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc about 375 ms); no changes.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with an underlying regular cycle of about 980 ms interrupted by one premature beat and a compensatory pause (RR 540 then 1370 ms); P waves precede the sinus beats with a PR interval of about 194 ms. QRS 98 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -31 degrees, i.e. borderline left axis deviation. QT about 354 ms with Bazett QTc about 358 ms (normal). There is no atrial fibrillation on this tracing, although paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is on the problem list. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

Regular sinus rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 838-884 ms) with an atrial deflection before every QRS at a constant PR interval of about 144 ms. QRS 88 ms with no bundle branch block. The frontal plane shows a globally negative lead I and aVL with a strongly positive aVR and negative aVF, giving a computed axis of about -173 degrees (extreme axis deviation); together with the inverted P wave in lead I and normal precordial R-wave progression this pattern is typical of right/left arm lead reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation, and repeat recording with correct electrode placement is advised. QT about 357 ms, Bazett QTc about 384 ms (normal, reassuring on escitalopram). This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, regular (RR 800-890 ms), with upright P waves and PR about 162 ms. QRS 100 ms - slightly wide but not meeting bundle branch block criteria; frontal axis about +37 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with broad T waves: QT about 509 ms and Bazett QTc about 550 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in a patient on citalopram 40 mg daily. The prior ECG of 6/17/2020 showed sinus tachycardia at 132 bpm with QTc about 435 ms, so the corrected QT has increased by about 115 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60). Rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular (RR 858-904 ms), with upright P waves in II/aVF and PR about 160 ms. QRS narrow at 80 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +57 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is abnormal and prolonged, with biphasic/low-amplitude T waves in the lateral and inferior leads and deep T inversion in V2-V3; tangent-method measurement across leads gives QT about 503 ms and a Bazett QTc of about 536 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in a patient taking escitalopram. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm, regular (RR 1112-1168 ms), with upright P waves and a PR interval of about 178 ms (normal). QRS 88 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -6 degrees (normal). QT about 381 ms with Bazett QTc about 358 ms (normal). The prior ECG of 12/13/2018 showed sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with a longer PR of about 216 ms (first-degree AV block) and QTc about 389 ms; rhythm, bundle branch conduction and QTc show no reportable change.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm (RR 862-902 ms) with normal upright P waves, PR about 132 ms. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +46 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is markedly prolonged: QT about 487 ms giving a Bazett QTc of about 519 ms, above the 500 ms threshold while the patient takes escitalopram. The prior ECG of 11/23/2022 showed sinus rhythm at 75 bpm with QTc about 354 ms, so the QTc has increased by about 165 ms - a QTC_INCREASE_60 change. Rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 141 bpm. The RR interval is now regular (402-454 ms) and a discrete low-amplitude upright P wave is identifiable in II/aVF before every QRS, well after the end of the T wave, with a PR interval of about 110 ms; atrial and ventricular rates are 1:1, so this is not atrial flutter. QRS 80 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -2 degrees (normal). QT about 271 ms, Bazett QTc about 415 ms. The prior ECG of 7/11/2022 showed atrial fibrillation at about 110 bpm with a chaotically irregular RR interval (380-824 ms) and no P waves, so the atrial fibrillation has resolved (RESOLVED_AF). QTc is unchanged (about 418 to 415 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, regular (RR 710-744 ms), with upright P waves and PR about 184 ms (normal). QRS 100 ms - mildly widened but not meeting criteria for right or left bundle branch block; frontal axis about +34 degrees (normal). QT about 372 ms with Bazett QTc about 437 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, regular (RR 650-668 ms), with upright P waves in II and aVF. The PR interval is prolonged at about 210-225 ms, consistent with first-degree AV block. QRS is narrow at 78 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -18 degrees (normal). QT about 338 ms, Bazett QTc about 417 ms. The prior ECG of 5/16/2021 showed sinus rhythm at 87 bpm with a normal PR of about 152 ms, QRS 80 ms and QTc about 393 ms; the PR has lengthened but rhythm, bundle branch conduction and QTc show no reportable change category.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm (RR 954-1196 ms) with upright P waves and a prolonged PR interval of about 222 ms - first-degree AV block. The QRS is wide at 128 ms with a broad monophasic R wave in I, aVL and V6, delayed intrinsicoid deflection, absent septal q waves and deep QS complexes in V1-V3: left bundle branch block, with large voltages suggesting associated left ventricular hypertrophy. Frontal axis about -21 degrees (normal). QT about 431 ms, Bazett QTc about 435 ms. The prior ECG of 6/3/2024 showed the identical pattern (sinus 68 bpm, PR about 220 ms, QRS 128 ms with left bundle branch block, QTc about 441 ms), so there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus rhythm at 102 bpm, regular (RR 580-596 ms), with upright P waves and PR about 156 ms. QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +45 degrees (normal). QT about 312 ms with Bazett QTc about 406 ms (normal). The prior ECG of 3/18/2025 was essentially the same (sinus 102 bpm, PR about 140 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc about 400 ms); no changes.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm with a regular RR interval (492-500 ms) and a discrete upright P wave before each QRS, PR about 150 ms. QRS duration 86 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +68 degrees (normal). QT about 285 ms, Bazett QTc about 405 ms (normal). This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, regular, with upright P waves in II and aVF and PR about 158 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +58 degrees (normal). QT about 319 ms with Bazett QTc about 415 ms. The prior tracing taken 34 seconds earlier the same morning (102910502, 8/23/2021) was essentially identical (sinus 100 bpm, PR 152 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc about 408 ms), so there are no interval changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with a very regular RR interval (1144-1178 ms). Low-amplitude but clearly upright P waves in II/aVF (negative in V1) precede each QRS with a PR interval of about 176 ms, so this is sinus rather than a junctional rhythm; there is no AF despite the documented history of atrial fibrillation. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block, tall R waves in V6; frontal axis about +36 degrees (normal). QT about 435 ms, Bazett QTc about 404 ms. The prior ECG of 5/22/2023 also showed sinus rhythm (57 bpm with one premature beat, PR about 150 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc about 369 ms); no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, RR very regular (492-496 ms), upright P waves with PR about 136 ms. The QRS is now narrow at 92 ms with only a small terminal r in V1 (incomplete right bundle branch block pattern at most) and no complete bundle branch block. Prominent S waves in I and aVL with a net negative lead I give a rightward frontal axis of about +143 degrees. QT about 297 ms, Bazett QTc about 422 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (106516875, 01:33) showed a QRS of about 152 ms with a broad terminal R in V1 and wide S waves in I and V6 - complete right bundle branch block - which has resolved on this 14:38 tracing, hence RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK. QTc fell from about 476 to 422 ms (less than 60 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, regular (RR 944-982 ms), with upright P waves and PR about 184 ms (within normal limits). QRS 96 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +68 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is prolonged: QT about 528 ms with a Bazett QTc of about 537 ms, exceeding the 500 ms review threshold in a patient on amiodarone. The prior ECG of 6/7/2025 (sinus bradycardia 47 bpm, PR about 182 ms, QRS 96 ms, QTc about 407 ms) was taken before amiodarone was started, so the QTc has risen by about 130 ms - QTC_INCREASE_60. Rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

Atrial fibrillation with a moderately rapid, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean rate about 99 bpm (RR 386-1092 ms, RMSSD 264 ms). No organised P waves are seen in any lead and there is no consistent atrial deflection in the TP segments, so no measurable PR interval. QRS is narrow at 78 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -54 degrees (left axis deviation). QT about 328 ms, Bazett QTc about 421 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible. It corroborates the coded diagnosis of atrial fibrillation for which he is anticoagulated with warfarin.

arguments.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 66 bpm, regular (RR 902-932 ms), with upright P waves in II/aVF and a PR interval of about 168 ms. QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -21 degrees (normal). QT about 372 ms with Bazett QTc about 390 ms (normal). This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

items.explanation: 80-year-old woman with persistent atrial fibrillation documented in every cardiology clinic note (9/12/2025 through 5/28/2026). Chart also documents hypertensive heart disease with heart failure, type 2 diabetes, prior cerebral infarction/TIA and atherosclerotic coronary disease, giving CHA2DS2-VASc 9 (CHF 1, hypertension 1, age >=75 2, diabetes 1, prior stroke/TIA 2, vascular disease 1, female 1). Current medications are aspirin 81 mg and atorvastatin only, with no anticoagulant order active at the evaluation time. Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation (Class 1 for CHA2DS2-VASc >=2) is absent; antiplatelet therapy is not a substitute. Needs review for initiation of a DOAC or warfarin.

35-year-old woman on citalopram 40 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication; the current order runs 5/29/2026 to 12/25/2026 and the dose is above the 20 mg maximum usually advised when QT prolongation is present. Her most recent ECG (104821039, 11/10/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT about 509 ms and Bazett QTc about 550 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold; the previous ECG (6/17/2020) had a QTc of about 435 ms. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (1/21/2026) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (12/1/2023) are normal, and she also has hypothyroidism and type 1 diabetes. Prescriber review of citalopram dose and a current ECG are required.

44-year-old man with coronary disease and a coronary stent on escitalopram 10 mg daily, a QT watch-list medication; the current order runs 7/8/2026 to 12/29/2026. His most recent (and only) ECG (101538691, 3/8/2026, obtained as the post-start monitoring ECG) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with markedly abnormal repolarisation, QT about 503 ms and Bazett QTc about 536 ms, above the 500 ms review threshold. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L and magnesium 1.9 mg/dL (4/8/2026) are normal. Prescriber review of escitalopram and a repeat ECG are required.

95-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation/flutter on long-term amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug; the current order runs 8/22/2026 to 1/5/2027. Her most recent ECG (101515306, 4/27/2022) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with first-degree AV block (PR about 210 ms), QT about 537 ms and Bazett QTc about 526 ms, above the 500 ms review threshold (the 4/6/2022 tracing in AF had a QTc of about 421 ms). Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (2/14/2026) are at the low-normal end. She also takes metoprolol and warfarin. Prescriber review of amiodarone and an up-to-date ECG are required.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (a QT watch-list drug) was newly started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 3/2/2026. Because the start was on or after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, i.e. by 3/16/2026. ECG 104882441 was recorded on 3/7/2026 (sinus rhythm 81 bpm, QTc about 381 ms), 5 days after the start, so the requirement was met within the required time.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 11/10/2025. The start date falls between 9/1/2025 and 3/1/2026, so the 9/1/2025 memo's 30-day window applies and an ECG was due by 12/10/2025. ECG 106885519 was recorded on 11/24/2025, 14 days after the start, so the monitoring requirement was completed in time. (That ECG showed QTc about 537 ms and is the basis of a separate QT safety item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2/12/2026. The start predates 3/1/2026, so the 30-day window of the 9/1/2025 memo applies and an ECG was due by 3/14/2026. ECG 101538691 was recorded on 3/8/2026, 24 days after the start, meeting the requirement in time. (Its QTc of about 536 ms is the basis of a separate QT safety item.)

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 4/10/2026. Because the start was after 3/1/2026 the revised memo applies and an ECG was due within 14 days, by 4/24/2026. No ECG exists in that window: the only tracing (107859369) was not recorded until 4/29/2026, 19 days after the start and outside the required window, so the requirement was not satisfied on time and remains past due for documentation/review. The 4/29/2026 ECG itself showed sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with QTc about 384 ms.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/1/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/15/2026. No ECG has been obtained since the start; the only tracing in the chart is 106035722 from 12/25/2025, which predates the start. The required post-start ECG is overdue as of the 9/24/2026 evaluation.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 8/10/2026, so under the revised memo an ECG was due within 14 days, by 8/24/2026. No ECG for this patient exists in the chart, but the nurse telephone note of 8/25/2026 records that the patient had an ECG at Northside Urgent Care on 8/18/2026 and that the report was requested by fax but not yet received. That outside tracing falls inside the required window and could have satisfied the requirement, so completion cannot be determined until the report arrives.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch-list drug) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 9/15/2026. Under the revised memo an ECG is due within 14 days of the start, i.e. by 9/29/2026. No ECG has been obtained since the start (the most recent tracing is 104253928 from 3/9/2025), but the due date is after the 9/24/2026 evaluation time, so the requirement is not yet due.

48-year-old man with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation documented in all cardiology clinic notes (7/19/2025 through 6/12/2026). Chart problem list includes congestive heart failure / acute systolic heart failure with other primary cardiomyopathy and essential hypertension, giving CHA2DS2-VASc 2 (CHF 1, hypertension 1; age 48, male, no diabetes, no prior stroke, no vascular disease). CHA2DS2-VASc >=2 in a man is a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation, but current medications are only famotidine and pantoprazole and no anticoagulant order is active at the evaluation time. Needs review for anticoagulation.

At the 9/1/2026 Cardiology Clinic visit Dr. Kessler documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily. Under the 3/1/2026 memo an INR was required within 7 days, i.e. by 9/8/2026. An INR of 2.3 was resulted on 9/5/2026 (Observation d6b3bad5), 4 days after the dose change, so the monitoring requirement was completed within the required time.

In the anticoagulation clinic telephone note of 9/10/2026 the clinic pharmacist (L. Nguyen, PharmD) decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per protocol after a home INR of 3.4. Clinic pharmacists may adjust warfarin under the standing order, so this is a qualifying dose change and the 3/1/2026 memo required an INR within 7 days, i.e. by 9/17/2026. No INR has been resulted since 8/22/2026 (INR 2.6); the home INR of 3.4 preceded and prompted the change and cannot satisfy it. The follow-up INR is overdue as of the 9/24/2026 evaluation.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on the problem list and in every cardiology clinic note (10/10/2025 through 7/28/2026). Risk factors: essential hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, coronary atherosclerosis of a native coronary artery (vascular disease) 1 = CHA2DS2-VASc 3, a Class 1 indication for oral anticoagulation. His only current medication is tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily; no anticoagulant order is active at the evaluation time. The chart carries a remote coded diagnosis of hemorrhage complicating a procedure, but no active bleeding or documented decision to withhold anticoagulation, so this needs prescriber review.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on the problem list. She also carries cerebral infarction due to embolism with residual hemiplegia/hemiparesis and facial weakness, and essential hypertension, giving CHA2DS2-VASc 5 (prior stroke 2, hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female 1). Anticoagulation is strongly recommended (Class 1, secondary stroke prevention), but current medications are famotidine, metoprolol tartrate and carvedilol only, with no anticoagulant order active at the evaluation time. Her 3/14/2025 ECG showed sinus rhythm, which does not change the indication in paroxysmal AF. Needs review for anticoagulation.

74-year-old man with atrial flutter on apixaban 5 mg twice daily; the current order was written 8/20/2026 and runs to 12/28/2026. Outside records reviewed on 8/12/2026 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer with haemoglobin nadir 6.9 g/dL and 2 units transfused, and state that apixaban was held at discharge pending cardiology review. Despite that, apixaban was re-ordered at the 8/20/2026 clinic visit (and he also remains on aspirin 81 mg plus clopidogrel 75 mg, i.e. triple therapy) with no documented decision that the bleeding source was treated or that anticoagulation could safely resume. Prescriber review of whether to continue apixaban, and of concomitant antiplatelet therapy, is required.

Two oral anticoagulants are simultaneously active for this 65-year-old man with paroxysmal/persistent atrial fibrillation and flutter. At the 7/15/2026 cardiology clinic visit the plan was to switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban for insurance coverage, but the rivaroxaban 20 mg daily order (7/15/2026 to 12/25/2026) was left active alongside the new apixaban 5 mg twice daily order (7/15/2026 to 12/26/2026), and the visit note lists both drugs as current medications. Both orders still cover the evaluation date, so the patient is prescribed duplicate full-dose anticoagulation with a high bleeding risk (he also has CLL). The rivaroxaban order must be discontinued.

The 6/10/2026 cardiology clinic note states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both 12-lead ECGs recorded that same day (107914094 at 17:13 and 103088543 at 19:36) show an irregularly irregular rhythm with no discernible P waves and ventricular rates of about 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, not sinus rhythm at 72. The documented rhythm and rate are contradicted by the same-day tracings; the chart rhythm documentation needs correction and the rapid AF needs clinical review.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily is a QT watch-list medication and the current order (4/23/2026 to 1/2/2027) is active at the evaluation time. His most recent ECG (108018814, 10/8/2023) shows sinus rhythm at 68 bpm with QT about 487 ms and Bazett-corrected QTc about 519 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the QT monitoring memo. Most recent electrolytes are normal (potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL, both 8/23/2025). The 5/14/2024 note describing the 10/8/2023 ECG as having an acceptable QT is not consistent with this measurement. Prescriber review of escitalopram and a repeat ECG are required.

79-year-old man with atrial fibrillation on amiodarone 200 mg daily, a QT watch-list drug; the current order runs 7/29/2026 to 1/5/2027. His most recent ECG (106885519, 11/24/2025) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT about 528 ms and Bazett QTc about 537 ms, above the 500 ms review threshold; the preceding ECG (6/7/2025, before amiodarone was started) had a QTc of about 407 ms, so this is a marked drug-associated increase. Most recent potassium 4.4 mEq/L and magnesium 2.2 mg/dL (4/20/2026) are normal. He is also on warfarin (amiodarone interaction). Prescriber review of amiodarone dosing and repeat ECG required.

interpretations.explanation: Sinus rhythm at 81 bpm with mild sinus arrhythmia (RR 656-856 ms). Upright P waves in II/aVF preceding every QRS, PR about 198 ms (upper normal, no AV block). Narrow QRS 78 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +47 degrees (normal). QT about 329 ms, Bazett QTc about 381 ms - normal despite concurrent citalopram. No prior ECG in the chart for comparison. Matches the 3/7/2026 clinic note documenting sinus rhythm.

Sinus rhythm at 104 bpm, regular (RR 568-586 ms), with well-formed upright P waves in II and aVF and PR about 148 ms - no atrial fibrillation on this tracing despite the documented paroxysmal AF. QRS 94 ms without bundle branch block; frontal axis about +38 degrees (normal). QT about 356 ms with Bazett QTc about 467 ms, borderline prolonged. On the prior ECG of 6/20/2025 (sinus tachycardia 147 bpm, PR about 124 ms, QRS 94 ms) the QTc was about 385 ms, so the corrected QT has increased by about 80 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60); rhythm and conduction are unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 109 bpm with a regular RR interval and an upright P wave before each QRS, PR about 128 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +36 degrees (normal). QT about 338 ms giving a Bazett QTc of about 456 ms, at the upper limit of normal and partly rate-related. Only one ECG exists for this patient, so no prior comparison is possible.

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 144 bpm and an irregularly irregular RR interval (348-650 ms). There are no P waves and no organised atrial activity, so the PR interval is not measurable. QRS 96 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -1 degree (normal). QT about 282 ms, Bazett QTc about 437 ms. The prior tracing from earlier the same evening (107914094, 6/10/2026 17:13) already showed atrial fibrillation at about 139 bpm with QTc about 437 ms, so there is no interval or rhythm change between them. Note that the 6/10/2026 clinic note recorded 'normal sinus rhythm, rate 72', which both same-day tracings contradict.

Regular narrow-complex rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 864-884 ms) with a low-amplitude atrial deflection before every QRS at a constant PR interval of about 148 ms - sinus rhythm; the P wave is upright in lead I but flat to slightly negative in II/aVF, suggesting a low atrial/leftward P axis or limb-lead placement variation rather than a change of mechanism. QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -25 degrees (normal). QT about 408 ms, Bazett QTc about 437 ms. The prior ECG of 4/27/2025 showed the same sinus mechanism at 60 bpm (QRS 80 ms, QTc about 405 ms) but with a markedly different, extreme frontal axis consistent with limb-lead reversal on that tracing; rhythm, conduction and QTc are otherwise unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 97 bpm, regular (RR 596-630 ms), with upright P waves and a PR interval of about 120 ms. QRS is narrow at 72 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +4 degrees (normal). QT about 299 ms with Bazett QTc about 381 ms (normal). This is the only ECG in the chart for this patient, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 72 bpm, regular (RR 820-840 ms), with upright P waves in II and aVF and PR about 152 ms. QRS 82 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +22 degrees (normal). The T wave is followed by a low-amplitude U wave, but tangent-method measurement in multiple leads gives QT about 375 ms and a Bazett QTc of about 411 ms, i.e. normal and below the 500 ms watch-list threshold. Only one ECG exists for this patient, so no prior comparison is possible; it predates the 8/1/2026 escitalopram start.

Atrial fibrillation with a slow, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean rate about 53 bpm (RR 694-1164 ms). Examination of every TP segment shows no P wave and only coarse fibrillatory undulation, so no PR interval is measurable; the apparent pre-QRS deflections on the short cycles are the tail of the preceding T wave. QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +29 degrees (normal). QT about 462 ms, Bazett QTc about 435 ms. The prior ECG of 11/12/2024 showed sinus rhythm at 69 bpm with clear P waves and PR about 192 ms, so atrial fibrillation is new on this tracing (NEW_AF).

Sinus bradycardia at 58 bpm with mild sinus arrhythmia (RR 976-1082 ms) and upright P waves before each QRS, PR about 116 ms. QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +60 degrees (normal). QT about 388 ms, Bazett QTc about 382 ms (normal), which is reassuring given the newly started haloperidol. The prior ECG of 3/8/2025 was also sinus (62 bpm, PR about 120 ms, QRS 84 ms, QTc about 425 ms); no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Sinus rhythm at 83 bpm, extremely regular (RR 716-726 ms), with upright P waves and PR about 160 ms. QRS narrow at 70 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +53 degrees (normal). QT about 341 ms with Bazett QTc about 402 ms (normal). This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 77 bpm, regular (RR 774-804 ms), with prominent upright P waves in II/aVF and PR about 174 ms. QRS is narrow at 68 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +64 degrees (normal). QT about 399 ms with Bazett QTc about 451 ms. The prior ECG of 2/2/2020 showed sinus rhythm at 75 bpm with a wider QRS of about 110 ms (not meeting bundle branch block criteria), diffusely inverted low-amplitude T waves and a much longer QTc of about 530-550 ms; the corrected QT has therefore shortened by roughly 80-100 ms (QTC_DECREASE_60). Rhythm is unchanged and no bundle branch block is present on either tracing.

Sinus tachycardia at 120 bpm, RR almost perfectly regular (494-504 ms) with a consistent upright P wave before each QRS, PR about 170 ms. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +51 degrees (normal). QT about 275 ms, QTc (Bazett) about 389 ms. Compared with the prior tracing of 9/16/2016 (sinus tachycardia 108 bpm, PR 182 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc about 396 ms) there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus bradycardia at 54 bpm, regular (RR 1074-1116 ms), with upright P waves in II and aVF. The PR interval is prolonged at about 220 ms, i.e. first-degree AV block. QRS 82 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +7 degrees (normal). QT about 401 ms, Bazett QTc about 382 ms (normal). The prior ECG of 11/30/2024 was also sinus bradycardia at 51 bpm with a borderline PR of about 200 ms, QRS 82 ms and QTc about 363 ms; rhythm, bundle branch conduction and QTc are unchanged (first-degree AV block is not one of the reportable change categories).

Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, mean rate about 153 bpm and a chaotically irregular RR interval (288-580 ms). No P waves or organised atrial activity are present, so the PR interval is not measurable. QRS 98 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -20 degrees (normal). QT about 271 ms with Bazett QTc about 432 ms. The prior ECG from the previous evening (107374881, 9/12/2025) showed sinus rhythm at 77 bpm with clear P waves, PR about 158 ms and one premature beat, so atrial fibrillation is new (NEW_AF). QTc is essentially unchanged (about 414 to 432 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 73 bpm with mild sinus arrhythmia (RR 788-922 ms), upright P waves in II/aVF and PR about 178 ms. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +11 degrees (normal). QT about 359 ms, Bazett QTc about 397 ms (normal). The prior ECG of 11/21/2025 was also sinus (67 bpm, PR about 158 ms, QRS 90 ms) but with a much longer QT (about 505 ms) and QTc of about 535 ms, so the corrected QT has shortened by roughly 140 ms (QTC_DECREASE_60). Rhythm and conduction are unchanged; this tracing agrees with the 11/23/2025 note documenting sinus rhythm.

Sinus rhythm at 74 bpm, regular (RR 780-840 ms), with upright P waves and a PR interval of about 190 ms (upper normal, not first-degree AV block). QRS 84 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +54 degrees (normal). QT about 372 ms with Bazett QTc about 413 ms (normal). This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus tachycardia at 112 bpm with an almost fixed RR interval (536-542 ms) and a clear upright P wave before every QRS, PR about 176 ms; there is no atrial flutter on this tracing despite the coded history of atrial flutter (no sawtooth waves, and the atrial and ventricular rates are 1:1). QRS 92 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +35 degrees (normal). QT about 279 ms, Bazett QTc about 381 ms. The prior ECG of 7/4/2022 was essentially identical (sinus tachycardia 115 bpm, PR about 182 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc about 375 ms); no changes.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm with an underlying regular cycle of about 980 ms interrupted by one premature beat and a compensatory pause (RR 540 then 1370 ms); P waves precede the sinus beats with a PR interval of about 194 ms. QRS 98 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -31 degrees, i.e. borderline left axis deviation. QT about 354 ms with Bazett QTc about 358 ms (normal). There is no atrial fibrillation on this tracing, although paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is on the problem list. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

Regular sinus rhythm at 69 bpm (RR 838-884 ms) with an atrial deflection before every QRS at a constant PR interval of about 144 ms. QRS 88 ms with no bundle branch block. The frontal plane shows a globally negative lead I and aVL with a strongly positive aVR and negative aVF, giving a computed axis of about -173 degrees (extreme axis deviation); together with the inverted P wave in lead I and normal precordial R-wave progression this pattern is typical of right/left arm lead reversal rather than true extreme axis deviation, and repeat recording with correct electrode placement is advised. QT about 357 ms, Bazett QTc about 384 ms (normal, reassuring on escitalopram). This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 70 bpm, regular (RR 800-890 ms), with upright P waves and PR about 162 ms. QRS 100 ms - slightly wide but not meeting bundle branch block criteria; frontal axis about +37 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is markedly prolonged with broad T waves: QT about 509 ms and Bazett QTc about 550 ms, well above the 500 ms threshold in a patient on citalopram 40 mg daily. The prior ECG of 6/17/2020 showed sinus tachycardia at 132 bpm with QTc about 435 ms, so the corrected QT has increased by about 115 ms (QTC_INCREASE_60). Rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm, regular (RR 858-904 ms), with upright P waves in II/aVF and PR about 160 ms. QRS narrow at 80 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +57 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is abnormal and prolonged, with biphasic/low-amplitude T waves in the lateral and inferior leads and deep T inversion in V2-V3; tangent-method measurement across leads gives QT about 503 ms and a Bazett QTc of about 536 ms, above the 500 ms threshold in a patient taking escitalopram. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus bradycardia at 53 bpm, regular (RR 1112-1168 ms), with upright P waves and a PR interval of about 178 ms (normal). QRS 88 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -6 degrees (normal). QT about 381 ms with Bazett QTc about 358 ms (normal). The prior ECG of 12/13/2018 showed sinus rhythm at 66 bpm with a longer PR of about 216 ms (first-degree AV block) and QTc about 389 ms; rhythm, bundle branch conduction and QTc show no reportable change.

Sinus rhythm at 68 bpm (RR 862-902 ms) with normal upright P waves, PR about 132 ms. QRS 90 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +46 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is markedly prolonged: QT about 487 ms giving a Bazett QTc of about 519 ms, above the 500 ms threshold while the patient takes escitalopram. The prior ECG of 11/23/2022 showed sinus rhythm at 75 bpm with QTc about 354 ms, so the QTc has increased by about 165 ms - a QTC_INCREASE_60 change. Rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

Sinus tachycardia at 141 bpm. The RR interval is now regular (402-454 ms) and a discrete low-amplitude upright P wave is identifiable in II/aVF before every QRS, well after the end of the T wave, with a PR interval of about 110 ms; atrial and ventricular rates are 1:1, so this is not atrial flutter. QRS 80 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -2 degrees (normal). QT about 271 ms, Bazett QTc about 415 ms. The prior ECG of 7/11/2022 showed atrial fibrillation at about 110 bpm with a chaotically irregular RR interval (380-824 ms) and no P waves, so the atrial fibrillation has resolved (RESOLVED_AF). QTc is unchanged (about 418 to 415 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 82 bpm, regular (RR 710-744 ms), with upright P waves and PR about 184 ms (normal). QRS 100 ms - mildly widened but not meeting criteria for right or left bundle branch block; frontal axis about +34 degrees (normal). QT about 372 ms with Bazett QTc about 437 ms. This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm at 91 bpm, regular (RR 650-668 ms), with upright P waves in II and aVF. The PR interval is prolonged at about 210-225 ms, consistent with first-degree AV block. QRS is narrow at 78 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -18 degrees (normal). QT about 338 ms, Bazett QTc about 417 ms. The prior ECG of 5/16/2021 showed sinus rhythm at 87 bpm with a normal PR of about 152 ms, QRS 80 ms and QTc about 393 ms; the PR has lengthened but rhythm, bundle branch conduction and QTc show no reportable change category.

Sinus rhythm at 61 bpm (RR 954-1196 ms) with upright P waves and a prolonged PR interval of about 222 ms - first-degree AV block. The QRS is wide at 128 ms with a broad monophasic R wave in I, aVL and V6, delayed intrinsicoid deflection, absent septal q waves and deep QS complexes in V1-V3: left bundle branch block, with large voltages suggesting associated left ventricular hypertrophy. Frontal axis about -21 degrees (normal). QT about 431 ms, Bazett QTc about 435 ms. The prior ECG of 6/3/2024 showed the identical pattern (sinus 68 bpm, PR about 220 ms, QRS 128 ms with left bundle branch block, QTc about 441 ms), so there is no change in rhythm, conduction or QTc.

Sinus rhythm at 102 bpm, regular (RR 580-596 ms), with upright P waves and PR about 156 ms. QRS 86 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +45 degrees (normal). QT about 312 ms with Bazett QTc about 406 ms (normal). The prior ECG of 3/18/2025 was essentially the same (sinus 102 bpm, PR about 140 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc about 400 ms); no changes.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm with a regular RR interval (492-500 ms) and a discrete upright P wave before each QRS, PR about 150 ms. QRS duration 86 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +68 degrees (normal). QT about 285 ms, Bazett QTc about 405 ms (normal). This is the only ECG in the chart, so no prior comparison is possible.

Sinus rhythm/mild sinus tachycardia at 102 bpm, regular, with upright P waves in II and aVF and PR about 158 ms. QRS 88 ms, no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +58 degrees (normal). QT about 319 ms with Bazett QTc about 415 ms. The prior tracing taken 34 seconds earlier the same morning (102910502, 8/23/2021) was essentially identical (sinus 100 bpm, PR 152 ms, QRS 90 ms, QTc about 408 ms), so there are no interval changes.

Sinus bradycardia at 52 bpm with a very regular RR interval (1144-1178 ms). Low-amplitude but clearly upright P waves in II/aVF (negative in V1) precede each QRS with a PR interval of about 176 ms, so this is sinus rather than a junctional rhythm; there is no AF despite the documented history of atrial fibrillation. QRS 90 ms with no bundle branch block, tall R waves in V6; frontal axis about +36 degrees (normal). QT about 435 ms, Bazett QTc about 404 ms. The prior ECG of 5/22/2023 also showed sinus rhythm (57 bpm with one premature beat, PR about 150 ms, QRS 86 ms, QTc about 369 ms); no rhythm, conduction or significant QTc change.

Sinus tachycardia at 121 bpm, RR very regular (492-496 ms), upright P waves with PR about 136 ms. The QRS is now narrow at 92 ms with only a small terminal r in V1 (incomplete right bundle branch block pattern at most) and no complete bundle branch block. Prominent S waves in I and aVL with a net negative lead I give a rightward frontal axis of about +143 degrees. QT about 297 ms, Bazett QTc about 422 ms. The earlier tracing the same day (106516875, 01:33) showed a QRS of about 152 ms with a broad terminal R in V1 and wide S waves in I and V6 - complete right bundle branch block - which has resolved on this 14:38 tracing, hence RESOLVED_BUNDLE_BRANCH_BLOCK. QTc fell from about 476 to 422 ms (less than 60 ms).

Sinus rhythm at 62 bpm, regular (RR 944-982 ms), with upright P waves and PR about 184 ms (within normal limits). QRS 96 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about +68 degrees (normal). Repolarisation is prolonged: QT about 528 ms with a Bazett QTc of about 537 ms, exceeding the 500 ms review threshold in a patient on amiodarone. The prior ECG of 6/7/2025 (sinus bradycardia 47 bpm, PR about 182 ms, QRS 96 ms, QTc about 407 ms) was taken before amiodarone was started, so the QTc has risen by about 130 ms - QTC_INCREASE_60. Rhythm and conduction are otherwise unchanged.

Atrial fibrillation with a moderately rapid, irregularly irregular ventricular response, mean rate about 99 bpm (RR 386-1092 ms, RMSSD 264 ms). No organised P waves are seen in any lead and there is no consistent atrial deflection in the TP segments, so no measurable PR interval. QRS is narrow at 78 ms with no bundle branch block; frontal axis about -54 degrees (left axis deviation). QT about 328 ms, Bazett QTc about 421 ms.
